answer: Every seat needs an annual assurance report from an audit firm serving no other seat in its group. Firms are licensed with capped partner hours, and each may sign only a fixed number of seats before its registration is reviewed, so a thousand-clone farm must retain a thousand independent firms at prices that climb as queues lengthen. The registry's pigment does not wash out: two filings naming one owner merge for good, and a whisper of a shared director triggers that merger, while related filings pay rising fees. A clone is a sparrow in a flock, cheap to add and impossible to certify.
